title: Does the fractionation reversal undo its own shuffle?
reader_title: Can a rune grid and rearranged coordinates decode six pages?
reader_intro: Uses a keyword to arrange the rune alphabet in a six-by-five grid, replaces each rune with its row and column numbers, and tests ways to rearrange or shift those numbers, including whether a shuffle can be undone.
reader_finding: Repairing the shuffle reversal restored all planted messages, but the manuscript outputs that passed the word screen still contained invalid grid cells; none supplies a verified reading.
reader_limit: Only the stated grid, 14 keywords and six pages were checked; the word screen can reward fragments after dropping invalid cells, so a high score alone is not a reading.
question: What do the archived 6×5 keyword-grid routes produce on six intended LP2 pages, and does the archived columnar reversal invert its forward transform?
reader_question: Does this grid-and-shuffle method work on LP2?
summary: The archived reversal fails 476 of 588 planted round trips. A repaired inverse passes all 588, but neither route yields a verified page reading under the source’s limited keyword and width grid.
finding: The source names 1,260 settings; its own length rule skips 336, and 2 of the remaining 924 cross its vocabulary-score gate. Its raw IoC is bounded by 1, so the IoC >1.3 gate cannot fire. A separately labeled exact inverse produces 2 score-gated rows among 588 settings. Every gated setting has invalid grid cells. The correction repairs a transposition inverse; it does not identify the manuscript cipher.
limitations: Only 14 source keywords, six checked page streams, five split rules, seven natural-order column widths and two coordinate shifts. The source gate can reward a few words even when invalid cells were dropped; raw IoC is not normalized or controlled. No general fractionation or plaintext verdict.
next_steps: Specify a coordinate-stream encoding, a single keyed transposition, null treatment and a held-out reading before interpreting further keyword matches.

scope.representation: Source GP29 rune order; 6×5 keyword-first table with the last cell empty. Archived source page_38/39/40/44/45/47 rune streams independently match the corresponding current LP2 pages under the source parser.
scope.procedure: Replay split, archived column reversal, direct and coordinate-shift routes exactly. Separately correct natural-order column lengths and compare 588 full-message planted round trips.
scope.parameters: 14 source keywords; six source-intended LP2 pages; split n/n−5/n+5/n//2/2n//3; widths 7,11,13,17,19,23,29; sub/add coordinate shifts.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, keys, keyed column orders, coordinate-stream encodings, alternate null handling, source bonus running-key methods and any decryption claim.

review.kind: source-defined bounded replay plus separately identified inverse repair
review.reviewer: All 1,512 scored routes checked against AST-extracted pinned source functions; 588 planted controls and exact page parser alignments

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; optional pinned Wulfic Git checkout for source-function parity audit.
